Class ExpressionParser

java.lang.Object
org.cyclops.integrateddynamics.core.evaluate.expression.tree.ExpressionParser
public final class ExpressionParser extends Object
Parses the text form of expressions, as written by ExpressionPrinter.printExact(Expression, ValueDeseralizationContext, IntFunction, Function, IntFunction). 
expression     := [parameters "=>"] ternary
parameters     := NAME | "(" parameter ("," parameter)* ")"
parameter      := NAME [":" [NAME ":"] NAME]
ternary        := or ["?" ternary ":" ternary]
or             := and ("||" and)*
and            := equality ("&&" equality)*
equality       := relational (("==" | "!=") relational)*
relational     := additive (("<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=") additive)*
additive       := multiplicative (("+" | "-") multiplicative)*
multiplicative := unary (("*" | "/" | "%") unary)*
unary          := "!" unary | ("-" NUMBER | primary) ("." NAME arguments)*
primary        := NUMBER | STRING | "true" | "false" | "@" TYPE SNBT | "#" (ID | NAME | STRING) | "?"
                | "[" [ternary ("," ternary)* [","]] "]" | NAME arguments | NAME | "(" (NAME | SYMBOL) ")" | "(" ternary ")"
arguments      := "(" [ternary ("," ternary)*] ")"
Operator names are resolved by OperatorNames, using the type of the first argument. A ? is an empty slot, and (name) an operator used as a value. As in Integrated Scripting, a.f(b) is f(a, b), calling a parameter as in f(a) is apply(f, a), + joins strings, strings can be in single quotes, and ->, === and !== can be written for =>, == and !=.

    • tokenize

      public static ExpressionParser.Tokenized tokenize(String text, ExpressionParser.Context context) throws ExpressionParseException
      Parse the text of an expression, and split the text into tokens that tell what node each part belongs to, as ExpressionPrinter.tokenizeExact(Expression, ValueDeseralizationContext, IntFunction, Function, ExpressionTypeChecker.Result) does for printed text, so typed text can be shown as typed.
      Parameters:
      text - The text of an expression.
      context - What the parser needs to know about the world.
      Returns:
      The expression and the tokens of the text.
      Throws:
      ExpressionParseException - If the text is not a valid expression.
